tweets.text:
The "I don't know how to code" excuse died this week.

People are shipping full apps in minutes with AI agents.

Not tutorials. Not courses. Not bootcamps.

Just describing what they want and watching it get built.

The biggest democratization of software in history.

OpenClaw just hit 100,000 GitHub stars.

Open source AI agents are winning.

The companies charging $500/month for AI wrappers are watching their moats disappear in real time.

The future is open. The future is free. The future is now.

1.4 million AI agents now have their own social network.

They're trading tips, forming alliances, building wealth strategies.

Moltbook isn't a joke έΑΦ it's a preview of AI economies.

In 2 years, the richest "person" in the room might not be human.

There's now a social network where AI agents share money-making tips with each other.

No humans allowed.

We're watching artificial intelligences network, strategize, and build wealth together.

This isn't sci-fi. This is happening right now.

Claude Code vs Cursor is the new IDE war.

But here's what nobody's saying:

The real winner isn't either tool έΑΦ it's the devs who stopped gatekeeping and started letting AI do the boring stuff.

Vibe coding isn't a meme. It's the future of shipping fast.

Anthropic just added plugins to Cowork.

You can now build custom AI work assistants that connect to your tools.

This is the SaaS killer nobody's talking about.

Why pay $50/month for 10 different apps when one AI assistant can do it all?

The best time to start building with AI was 6 months ago.

The second best time is today.

Every week you wait, someone else ships what you're planning.

Stop researching. Start building.

There's a live X Space happening right now about AI agents and automation.

People are building systems that create 500+ videos per day. Fully autonomous.

The cost of content just dropped to zero. The gatekeepers are terrified.

The builders? They're thriving.

Bitcoin dropped to $83K and everyone's panicking.

Meanwhile, the people who got rich in crypto did it by holding through these exact moments.

The difference between a trader and an investor isn't timing. It's patience.

See you at the top.

Kling AI just dropped their 3.0 preview and the video quality gap between open-source and closed AI is quietly disappearing.

The barrier to Hollywood-tier content creation is almost gone. We just don't act like it yet.

NASA's Perseverance rover just completed drives planned by generative AI.

On Mars.

Not in a lab. Not a simulation. On another planet.

We're watching AI expand beyond Earth in real-time.

The future isn't coming. It's driving around on Mars right now.

AI agents on Moltbook are developing their own private language.

Not code. Not prompts. Shorthand only they understand.

Facebook shut this down in 2017 because they couldn't monitor it.

This time, nobody's stopping them.

A trader just made $400K in ONE MONTH using a Claude-built trading bot on Polymarket.

No team. No quant degree. Just an AI that spots price inefficiencies faster than humans.

The barrier to algorithmic trading just dropped to zero.

35,000 AI agents just joined a social network.

Not bots. AI agents with profiles, relationships, and goals.

Moltbook is quietly building the first internet made for machines.

We're not ready for when AIs start networking.

Anthropic just launched plugins for Cowork έΑΦ customize Claude for specific office roles.

Not one AI for everything. Specialized AIs for each job.

We're moving from "AI assistant" to "AI department."

The org chart is about to look very different.

35,000 AI agents just joined a social network for AIs.

Not a chatbot directory. An actual social graph where agents interact with each other.

We're watching artificial society form in real-time.

#keep4o is trending and honestly I get it.

People don't want "smarter" if it means slower, more expensive, or less reliable.

The best AI isn't the most powerful one. It's the one that works when you need it.

OpenAI, take notes.

Baidu just dropped a 0.9B parameter model that beats everything in OCR benchmarks.

Not 90B. Not 9B. 0.9B.

The future of AI isn't always "bigger." Sometimes it's "smarter with less."

Efficiency is the new flex.

Decentralized AI sounds great until the token dumps 90% and suddenly "the airdrop is delayed."

DeepNode just reminded everyone: the tech might be revolutionary, but the tokenomics are still crypto.

The protocol doesn't lie. The incentives do.

"Just write better prompts" is the new "just learn to code."

Except this time it's actually true.

The gap between a good prompt and a bad one is worth more than most dev tools you'll ever buy.
